signatures.black mark after electroplating: Discrete dark/black smudge or spot sitting on top of otherwise normal plating; local darkening not explained by shadow.
signatures.electroplating defect: Patch of abnormal/uneven plating - dull, matte or rough area where the finish did not deposit uniformly.
signatures.incomplete embossing: Stamped 'VA' logo is partial, faint or missing strokes; low central relief contrast.
signatures.line defect: A single distinct straight scratch/gouge line crossing the surface, standing out from the normal brushed micro-texture.
signatures.serration: Jagged/toothed edge on a hole that should be smooth (NOT the by-design splined bottom hole).
signatures.OK: Uniform finish, complete emboss, no discrete mark/line, smooth round hole edges.

lessons.note: Durable lessons learned from human corrections. Loaded into defect_kb.json on every rebuild so inspection never loses them. Covers the free-form cup-collar part (deep-drawn collar/cup) which has NO ground-truth polygons.

cup-collar.description: Deep-drawn metal collar / cup: outer flange (rolled edge), a stepped inner rim/collar, and a central bore. Photographed top-down (rim visible as a ring) or tilted (side view, rim foreshortened).

signatures.notch / nick on inner rim: A small raised nub or a bite/indentation breaking the smooth curve of the inner collar rim edge. Localised (a few mm). NOT the long bright rim highlight itself.
signatures.cut / chipped flange edge (missing mater: A bite of material missing from the outer rolled flange edge - the edge outline steps inward or looks torn/faceted instead of a smooth continuous curve.
signatures.dark mark / stain on bottom flange: Discrete dark/black smudge or burn sitting on top of the flange face; darker than the surrounding metal and NOT the shadow cast by the rim.
signatures.reject paint mark / rough flange edge: Deliberate red/pink inspection paint OR a locally rough, pitted, torn flange edge.
signatures.pinched / out-of-round bore: Central bore is not a clean circle - one side pinched, dented inward or ovalised.
signatures.square tab on inner rim (12 o'clock): A square/blocky tab interrupting the inner rim near the 12 o'clock position. CONFIRMED BY USER AS A DEFECT - flag it on every cup where it appears.
signatures.OK: Smooth continuous outer flange, unbroken inner rim curve, round bore, no discrete dark mark, no missing material.

confirmed_rulings: The square tab at ~12 o'clock on the inner rim IS a defect (not a by-design locating tab). Flag it every time.

Tilted / side-view cups whose inner rim is smooth and not clearly visible (e.g. 162751, 162819, 162618, 162900, 163000, 163031) are OK - do NOT paint a speculative box; a false mark is worse than none.
Scan the ENTIRE part for EVERY defect type seen anywhere in the set - full outer edge, inner rim, both flanges and faces. Never stop at the first finding.
A defect type seen on one cup (e.g. flange cut on 162340) must be looked for on ALL cups - cross-apply learned defect types.
Capture MULTIPLE defects per image and rank them; mark the highest-severity one as PRIMARY.

segmentation_gotchas: edge/Canny segmentation on a small feature that sits ON a bright curved rim will LOCK ONTO THE RIM and trace a long arc instead of the feature. For small notches/nicks on the inner rim, use a TINY tight box and DROP edge-seg (draw a plain rectangle). Root cause of repeated 'mask too big / wrong spot' complaints.
dark segmentation grabs the shadowed rim, not the actual stain, when the box is loose. Shrink the box below/away from the rim so the stain is the darkest pixel region.
Always place boxes tiny and tight on the actual defect, then verify each output at full zoom before reporting.

reject_paint_rule.principle: Red/pink reject paint is the operator's MARK showing WHERE they saw a problem - it is NOT itself the primary defect. When paint is present, HUNT the adjacent edge/geometry for the real defect (a cut, notch, dent, missing material) and mark THAT as primary; mark the paint only as a low-severity secondary.
reject_paint_rule.learned_from: IMG20260824162340 - I originally boxed the red paint + inner rim (most eye-catching) and edge-seg traced those instead of the real cut on the OUTER silhouette edge nearby.
reject_paint_rule.scan_habit: Trace the OUTER silhouette outline of the flange for steps/facets/kinks (missing material) - these are low-contrast against the smooth curve and easy to miss. Do not anchor only on bright bands or the paint.

recurring_mistakes: Stopping at the first defect per image instead of scanning the whole part.
Not cross-applying a defect type seen on one image to the others.
Misreading shallow cuts / dark marks as the part's natural pressed shape.
Placing boxes from downscaled previews and not verifying at full resolution.
